title: Busy Beaver functions

based_on.title: The Busy Beaver Frontier
based_on.pages: 31–55; selected sections 1–2, manuscript pp. 1–5; program-size variants and their proofs adapted to the shared recursive-program syntax

summary: Maximize outputs and successful computation resources over programs of bounded size, prove growth beyond every computable function, and recover the halting problem from either maximum.
abstract: Among all programs with at most a given amount of text, some halt and some run forever. The halting programs have a largest output and a largest resource needed to certify their computations. These Busy Beaver bounds are definite natural numbers, but neither bound can be computed uniformly from the permitted program size. The output bound eventually exceeds every total computable function, because a short program can first construct its input and then compute a still larger value. We prove this using the same recursive-program language as the universal evaluator, with size measured by the number of syntax nodes. We also show that either bound contains exactly the information of the ordinary halting problem: a halting oracle computes the finite maxima, and either maximum supplies enough information to decide whether an arbitrary computation halts.
